EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The most critical developments of the past 24 hours revolve around a new mutual defense pact in the Gulf, escalating tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, and an anticipated surge in regional proxy attacks. Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan have signed the "Mecca Joint Defense Agreement," while Iran claims to have engaged "hostile targets" at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz amid reports of an Iranian parliamentary bill to impose transit fees and restrict hostile vessels. Concurrently, Saudi intelligence warns of imminent coordinated attacks from Houthi rebels and pro-Iranian militias in Iraq against its economic infrastructure.

IRAN
Military operations by Iran include claims of engaging "hostile targets" at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz after two explosions were reported on Qeshm Island on August 5, 2026, at approximately 21:40 local time. The IRGC Aerospace Force claims to have downed a US F-15 fighter jet and other US-Israeli aircraft using a newly developed air defense system, and images of wreckage were published. Iran's parliament is weighing an 11-article bill to formalize control over the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf. This bill proposes prohibiting passage of vessels belonging to the US, Israel, and other hostile nations; banning military and non-military cargoes bound for or associated with Israel; denying transit to entities causing damage to Iran until financial compensation is paid; imposing fines of up to 20% of cargo value for violators; and mandating direct Iranian governmental and armed forces responsibility for navigation guidance, monitoring, and security.

On the internal political front, unverified reports from an opposition website, IranWire, suggest Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is in a "very critical condition" and may die soon, with no meetings between him and President Pezeshkian's government since the February 28 attack. Hardline clerics, such as Akhund Kharazi, have reportedly threatened to kill unveiled women and supporters of a "satanic government." Economic reports indicate a prolonged disruption, with no tankers observed loading at Kharg Island since July 31, the longest such event since the war began, attributed to a US naval blockade. Global food prices, including wheat, have risen significantly due to regional conflicts and weather. Iran is seeking transit fees between 5-7% of cargo value for ships using the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf has dismissed US President Trump's "theater diplomacy" as a failed strategy.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations included an artillery attack on Syria's Quneitra Province and artillery strikes on the towns of Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah and Al-Mansouri in southern Lebanon. Israeli forces also blew up homes of displaced residents in Kounine, southern Lebanon, and opened fire on the head of the Bint Jbeil Water Department and workers in Aita al-Jabal, south Lebanon. One Israeli soldier, Rassm (res.) Tamir Vaknin, was killed on August 6 in southern Lebanon by an IED. The US and Israel completed a joint missile defense system test.

Politically, Israel is reportedly resisting US pressure to tactically withdraw its concrete blocks defining expanded firing lines in Gaza, which now cover 70% of the Strip. This resistance stems from concerns that any withdrawal would appear as a retreat and negatively impact the Likud party and the coalition ahead of elections. US-brokered negotiations between Lebanon and Israel in Rome concluded without a breakthrough. The Mossad reportedly dismissed two senior officials, the head of the intelligence directorate and the head of the Iran department, over a failed plot to overthrow the Iranian government. Civilian incidents included a 30-year-old man killed in a Jerusalem traffic accident, two men severely injured in Tayibe, a 10-year-old boy injured by electrocution in Ar'ara BaNegev, a 60-year-old worker injured in Hadera, and a 50-year-old woman injured in Ashdod. Seven individuals, including four minors, are accused of murder in the July 11 Benyahu Razi case in Jerusalem, and three suspects have been identified in the murder of Muhammad Mahamid in Umm al-Fahm. A six-month-old infant died from suffocation by a bag in Bnei Brak, and a one-and-a-half-year-old girl drowned in Ashkelon. The New York Times reported claims of violence and abuse, including electric shocks, against over 20 activists who attempted to breach the Israeli blockade on Gaza, which Israel denies.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Ground operations in Gaza show that the IDF has expanded its control to 70% of the Strip, utilizing concrete blocks to establish firing lines. A Hamas Nukhba Force terrorist, who participated in the October 7, 2023, attack, was captured by the IDF on August 5 while working as a truck driver delivering private sector goods to the Israeli-held portion of the Gaza Strip, specifically at the Kerem Shalom Crossing. The humanitarian situation remains challenging, with reports from the UN's Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) indicating that global food prices have reached a three-year high, influenced by conflicts in the Gulf and Black Sea regions. The New York Times reported that more than 20 activists attempting to breach the Israeli blockade on Gaza described experiencing violence, electric shocks, and other forms of abuse after being apprehended, allegations which Israel denies. There were no direct reports of new casualties within Gaza.

Ceasefire or negotiation status remains uncertain, despite the US Treasury Secretary's statement that a deal, potentially including a 30-60 day ceasefire and the reopening of waterways, could be reached "soon, perhaps even today or tomorrow." However, US-brokered talks between Lebanon and Israel in Rome ended after three days without any perceptible progress. In the West Bank, an armed Israeli settler, backed by IOF, was filmed tying up and assaulting an elderly Palestinian during an incursion into the village of Bayt Iksa.

LEBANON
Hezbollah operations were referenced in Lebanese reports stating that a Hezbollah terrorist was killed while riding a motorcycle in Meifdon, southern Lebanon. Israeli forces conducted several strikes, including an artillery attack on Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah and Al-Mansouri in southern Lebanon, and were reported to have blown up homes of displaced residents in Kounine. Additionally, Israeli forces opened fire on the head of the Bint Jbeil Water Department and several workers carrying out maintenance in the town of Aita al-Jabal.

Cross-border exchanges led to the death of Israeli reservist Rassm (res.) Tamir Vaknin by an IED in southern Lebanon on August 6. Despite this, Israeli media reported that Washington, via intensive communications, urged Israel to de-escalate in Lebanon, confirming no breach by Hezbollah in southern Lebanon following the killing of two Israeli soldiers (it is unclear if this refers to the Vaknin incident or a separate event). Negotiations between Lebanon and Israel, brokered by the US in Rome, concluded after three days without any significant breakthrough.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Syria, Israeli forces launched an artillery attack on Quneitra Province while the Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan was visiting Damascus. This highlights ongoing regional rivalries.

In Iraq, pro-Iranian militias are reportedly coordinating with Houthi rebels in Yemen for imminent strikes against Saudi Arabia, targeting economic infrastructure such as ports, energy facilities, and airports. Iraqi security forces were deployed in Baghdad to prevent potential actions by Hashd al-Shaabi (a proxy of the IRGC) against Saudi Arabia. The Iraqi government has reaffirmed its commitment to the national policy of exclusive state control over weapons, stating there is no turning back on this path. However, armed clashes were reported in the Mansour area of Baghdad, following a shooting incident involving an anti-terrorism officer and a provincial council employee. The US Federal Reserve has reportedly sent a $500 million cash shipment to Iraq's Central Bank, which renews scrutiny over arrangements requiring Baghdad to seek Washington's approval to access its oil revenues. The Iraqi marine syndicate has protested a joint memorandum by Saudi Arabia and Kuwait to the UN regarding Iraqi maritime boundaries. Russian state media has noted strong relations between Hashd al-Shaabi and Russia, citing expressions of friendship and images of Putin in Baghdad, which has reportedly caused "strong dissatisfaction" at the US Embassy.

GULF STATES
The Gulf region is seeing significant shifts in alliances and escalating threats. Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan signed the "Mecca Joint Defense Agreement," a mutual defense pact declaring an attack on one as an attack on all. Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan stated this aims to create a safer regional environment. Despite this, Saudi Arabia is bracing for imminent coordinated attacks from Houthi rebels and pro-Iranian militias in Iraq, targeting critical economic infrastructure. Houthi attacks have already resulted in at least 30 Yemeni government soldiers killed in Marib and Hadramout provinces, and 11 civilians injured in Najran, Saudi Arabia. Kuwait has preemptively shut down oil wells near its Iraqi border due to fears of imminent attacks.

The UAE's national oil company, ADNOC, reported that 15 of its vessels have been attacked by missiles and drones in the Strait of Hormuz since the war began, with three incidents occurring in the last week. Russian President Vladimir Putin held a phone call with UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed to discuss the Middle East and Ukraine.

Regarding the Strait of Hormuz, Oman and Iran have agreed on a framework for a temporary deal to reopen the Strait to commercial vessels, with an official announcement expected pending non-interference from "certain third parties." Iran is reportedly seeking transit fees of 5-7% of cargo value, while Oman proposes 3%. However, this fee structure is deemed "impractical" by shipping industry sources due to US sanctions and insurance risks. The US maintains that no fees should be imposed. MarineTraffic data indicates a 33% reduction in confirmed transits through the Strait of Hormuz, with most traffic adhering to Iran's unilateral plan. US President Trump warned of risks to ships from mines in the Strait, further affecting oil prices.

Yemen's Supreme Political Council President Mehdi al-Mashat dismissed the Mecca pact as ineffective and reiterated the "blockade for blockade" strategy until its objectives are met. Iran's parliamentarian, Ibrahim Rezaei, criticized the Mecca pact, stating it would not bring security to Riyadh.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Mecca Joint Defense Agreement Signed:** Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan formally established a mutual defense alliance, pledging to treat an armed attack against any one of them as an attack against all.
2.  **Strait of Hormuz Tensions Escalate:** Two explosions occurred on Qeshm Island, Iran, with Iranian authorities claiming they engaged "hostile targets" at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's parliament is considering a bill to formalize control over the Strait, including imposing transit fees (5-7% of cargo value) and banning vessels from hostile nations.
3.  **Imminent Attacks on Saudi Arabia Anticipated:** Saudi officials report intelligence indicating coordinated and imminent missile and drone attacks by Houthi rebels in Yemen and pro-Iranian militias in Iraq against Saudi economic infrastructure. Houthi attacks have reportedly killed 30 Yemeni government soldiers and injured 11 civilians in Najran, Saudi Arabia.
4.  **Mossad Leadership Purge:** Israel's Mossad reportedly dismissed two top officials—the head of the intelligence directorate and the head of the Iran department—for their alleged failure in a plot to overthrow the Iranian government.
5.  **US Military Adjustments:** The US has begun relocating aerial refueling aircraft from Israeli-occupied territories due to ongoing strains from the war on Iran. Concurrently, a new US intelligence assessment suggests Russia might attempt a limited assault on a NATO member in the coming years.
6.  **Gaza Control and Terrorist Capture:** The IDF has expanded its control to 70% of the Gaza Strip. A Hamas Nukhba terrorist, who participated in the October 7 attack, was captured while driving an aid truck near the Kerem Shalom Crossing.
7.  **Lebanon Escalation Amid Failed Talks:** US-brokered negotiations between Lebanon and Israel in Rome ended without a breakthrough. Simultaneously, Israeli forces conducted intense artillery strikes in southern Lebanon, causing casualties and destroying homes. An Israeli soldier was killed by an IED in the area.
8.  **Stalled Iran-Oman Hormuz Deal:** A framework agreement between Iran and Oman to reopen the Strait of Hormuz for commercial vessels faces significant obstacles due to Iran's proposed transit fees, which conflict with US policy and pose legal and financial risks for international shipping.
9.  **Global Food Crisis Deepens:** The UN Food and Agriculture Organization reports that global food prices have reached a three-year high, driven by adverse weather conditions and escalating conflicts in the Gulf and Black Sea regions, with cereal prices notably increasing by 3.4% in June.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
**Escalation Risks:** The Strait of Hormuz is an active flashpoint with high escalation risks, evidenced by Iran's reported engagement with "hostile targets" and the proposed parliamentary bill to impose transit fees and restrict hostile vessels. This could lead to direct military confrontation. Saudi Arabia faces a high risk of imminent, coordinated attacks from Houthi rebels and pro-Iranian militias in Iraq, potentially targeting critical economic infrastructure. The conclusion of US-brokered Israel-Lebanon talks without a breakthrough, coupled with continued Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon and an Israeli casualty from an IED, indicates a high risk of further escalation on the Israeli-Lebanese border.
**Active Flashpoints:** The Strait of Hormuz, Marib and Hadramout provinces in Yemen, Najran in Saudi Arabia, and southern Lebanon remain highly active flashpoints. There is also increased alert along the Saudi-Iraq border due to potential activities by Iraqi militias.
**Military Posture Changes:** The formation of the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement by Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan represents a significant shift in regional alliances. The US relocating aerial refueling aircraft from Israeli-occupied territories signals a potential adjustment in its military footprint. Iraq's emphasis on exclusive state control over weapons, alongside the deployment of security forces in Baghdad to counter potential Hashd al-Shaabi actions against Saudi Arabia, reflects attempts to manage internal and external proxy threats. Iran's claims of successfully downing US F-15s and other US-Israeli aircraft highlight perceived improvements in its air defense capabilities.
**Red Lines:** Iran's proposed parliamentary bill on the Strait of Hormuz, if enacted, would establish new red lines for naval transit, including banning certain vessels and imposing fees. This directly conflicts with the US stance of no fees and could lead to direct challenges to freedom of navigation. Any large-scale coordinated attack on Saudi infrastructure by Houthi or Iraqi militias would likely trigger a robust response, potentially widening the conflict.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**US Posture:** President Trump publicly expressed satisfaction with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, dismissing reports of dissatisfaction and denying US munitions shortages, despite internal reports of a $21 billion replenishment request and CNN concerns about Patriot and THAAD interceptor stocks. He reportedly ordered an investigation into leaks about munitions. The US is relocating aerial refueling aircraft from Israel. The US Treasury Secretary anticipates a 30-60 day ceasefire deal for the region, including the opening of waterways, in the coming days.
**Gulf States:** Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan signed the "Mecca Joint Defense Agreement," a mutual defense pact. Saudi Arabia is on high alert for imminent attacks from Houthi rebels and Iraqi militias. The UAE's ADNOC reported 15 vessel attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. Kuwait has pre-emptively shut down oil wells on its Iraqi border. Oman and Iran agreed on a framework for a temporary deal on Strait of Hormuz transit, but disagreements on fees (Iran 5-7%, Oman 3%, US 0%) pose challenges.
**EU Members:** Spain threatened reciprocal measures against Italian tourists if Italy doesn't lift border checks, which Italy rejected. Germany faces significant political turmoil, with discussions about replacing Chancellor Friedrich Merz.
**Russia:** President Putin held a phone call with UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed to discuss regional conflicts. Russian intelligence assesses that Putin may attempt a limited assault on a NATO member state in the coming years. Russian state media highlights close ties with Iraq's Hashd al-Shaabi.
**China:** China's Foreign Ministry expressed readiness to strengthen law enforcement dialogue with the US on transnational crime.
**Turkey:** Signed the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement and FM Hakan Fidan visited Damascus. President Erdogan emphasized the Mecca pact is defensive and open to other regional countries.
**Yemen:** Mehdi al-Mashat, President of Yemen's Supreme Political Council, dismissed the Mecca pact as ineffective and reaffirmed the "blockade for blockade" strategy. Yemen's Foreign Ministry warned Saudi Arabia that continued "colonial policies" would lead to its collapse.
**Iraq:** The Iraqi military command announced a plan to prevent attacks on Saudi Arabia. Iraq's government reiterated its commitment to exclusive state control of weapons. The Iraqi marine syndicate protested Saudi and Kuwaiti claims regarding maritime boundaries to the UN.
**Iran:** An Iranian parliament member criticized the Mecca pact, urging Saudi Arabia to change its policies instead of relying on external agreements. Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Gharaibabadi confirmed documenting attacks from neighboring countries and vowed decisive responses to direct assaults.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
**Contradictions between sources:** US President Trump's public assertions of "unlimited" US munitions contrast with reports of a $21 billion request for replenishment and CNN's concerns over low Patriot and THAAD interceptor stocks. Similarly, Trump's public defense of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth conflicts with earlier CNN/Wall Street Journal reports detailing Trump's private anger over a munitions leak and an order for an investigation. Regarding the Strait of Hormuz, initial reports of a framework deal between Iran and Oman are complicated by conflicting details on transit fees (Iran's proposed 5-7%, Oman's 3%, and the US stance of no fees), with an Iranian opposition channel claiming the deal is "stalled." Houthi claims of "taromaring" (decimating) Saudi-backed forces in Yemen appear exaggerated when compared to more measured casualty reports.
**Unverified claims:** Reports regarding the critical health status of Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei originate from an opposition website (IranWire) and remain unconfirmed. Claims by Israeli media (and subsequently Press TV) about the dismissal of two senior Mossad officials for a failed plot to overthrow the Iranian government lack independent verification and specific details. Similarly, the claims of the IRGC Aerospace Force downing US F-15s and other US-Israeli aircraft, presented with images of wreckage by Iranian state media, require independent corroboration. A claim by Kian Meli 1 about US glide bombs hitting an air defense site on Kharg Island also remains unverified. An unnamed senior Saudi official's warning of imminent coordinated Houthi and Iraqi militia attacks on Saudi Arabia is a significant but uncorroborated intelligence assessment.
**Propaganda indicators:** Iranian state media (Press TV, Tasnim, SharghDaily) consistently frame US/Israeli actions as aggressive or failing, while portraying Iranian forces as highly capable and successful (e.g., claiming downed aircraft). Iranian opposition channels (Omid Dana, Kian Meli 1, Mamlekate) frequently highlight internal regime instability, economic hardship, and pro-Western narratives, often employing emotionally charged language. Israeli and Saudi-affiliated media focus on threats and defensive measures, aligning with national narratives.
**Reporting gaps:** Specific details about the "hostile targets" engaged by Iran off Qeshm Island are not provided. The full scope and specifics of the alleged "failed plot" to overthrow the Iranian government and the precise roles of the dismissed Mossad officials are not elaborated. Comprehensive, independently verified information on military engagements and claims from all parties involved remains limited. The full texts and implementation protocols for the Iran-Oman Strait of Hormuz deal and the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement are not available, leaving key details open to interpretation and dispute. The identity of the "certain third parties" Oman referred to as potentially interfering with the Hormuz deal is not specified.
